title: Proactive token throttling and SLO extrapolation for VPC deployments
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a proactive token-throttling subsystem plus an SLO-extrapolator for Private/VPC worker pools. Goals: 1) reduce customer-visible errors during token surges by applying graceful, predictive throttling and backpressure; 2) produce an SLO extrapolation signal (30m/1h/6h) that estimates likely violation probability for latency, error-rate, and token throughput SLOs; 3) expose IaC primitives (Terraform module + variables) so customers hosting Redwood Private can opt into the feature and tune thresholds centrally. This is targeted at on-prem/VPC worker fleets where autoscaling is constrained and token bursts cause tail-latency, saturations, and cascading errors. The feature must integrate with existing probe exporters and the Console SLO dashboards, and emit a new metric series for the extrapolated violation probability and the throttling decisions for auditing and postmortem.
acceptance_criteria: A1: A new metric 'vpc_token_throttle_decision' (labels: region, deployment, decision_reason) is emitted for each throttling action
A2: SLO-extrapolator publishes 'vpc_slo_violation_risk' with time horizons 30m,1h,6h and is visible in Grafana and Console SLO UI
A3: Terraform module 'redwood/vpc/token-throttle' created with variables for target_slo_bounds, conservative_mode, and dry_run
A4: Under a controlled token surge (test harness) worker error-rate and 95th latency degrade gracefully vs baseline by >=30% fewer customer errors
A5: Unit + integration tests covering extrapolator math, boundary conditions, and fail-open/fail-closed behaviors
A6: Security review completed for signal surface and audit logging; KMS keys for throttling audit payloads validated
implementation_steps: Design & math: finalize extrapolator algorithm (EWMA + quantile forecasting + conservative multiplier)
Prototype: implement a go-based service module in runtime/telemetry to compute violation risk windows
Metrics: add prometheus exporters for decision events and extrapolated risk time series
Control plane: extend vpc-agent to accept throttle policies and to apply token-level backpressure (per-tenant and per-route)
IaC: author terraform module with variables, examples, and upgrade notes; add acceptance tests in infra/terraform/tests
Console: wire new metrics into SLO dashboards and add a small UX affordance for 'live risk preview'
Rollout: dry-run rollout to staging VPC clusters -> limited canary -> region-wide opt-in
design_tradeoffs: Tradeoff: Conservative (fail-open) vs aggressive (fail-closed) throttling — default uses conservative_mode=true to minimize false positives
Tradeoff: Accuracy vs compute cost — extrapolator uses lightweight EWMA+quantile approach rather than full ARIMA/ML model to keep CPU footprint low on edge workers
Tradeoff: Centralized decisions vs local autonomy — policy allows local agent to make fast decisions with periodic central re-eval to avoid cross-region latency issues

testing_plan: Unit tests for extrapolator math (edge cases: zero-traffic, burst window, noisy signals)
Integration test: deploy terraform module to a staging VPC cluster and run token-burst harness (payload attached)
Load test: synthetic 500k-token burst across 50 workers; measure decision latencies and effectiveness vs control group
Canary: 5% of staging clusters get 'active' mode, others remain 'dry_run' to collect compare metrics
mitigation_plan: If the throttling logic causes unexpected customer errors, we will immediately flip the policy to dry_run (Terraform boolean) and deploy a fail-open hotfix to vpc-agent within 15 minutes. An incident runbook has a rollback play that removes the module's webhook and clears local decision cache; on-call SRE will be paged with runbook link.
release_notes: Added proactive token throttling and SLO-extrapolator for Private/VPC worker pools. Feature is behind a terraform-controlled toggle 'active' (default: false). Emits metrics: vpc_token_throttle_decision, vpc_slo_violation_risk. Requires runtime-1.21 and Console update for visualization.
